about: Draft research for a mock-up of the angels-and-demons page (“the unseen”), on Michael. Every quotation of Scripture is the site's KJV text; every other item carries its source. Not yet independently reviewed.

meanings.text: From mî “who”, the prefix “like”, and ’ēl “God”: “who (is) like God?” The name of an archangel and of nine Israelites.
“who like God?” … the name of an archangel, who was supposed to be the guardian angel of the Israelites.
“Who is like God? … The title given to one of the chief angels.”

outlier.text: Hitchcock's name dictionary, which the site uses for name meanings, lists Michael as “same as Micah” and glosses Micah “poor; humble”. The major lexicons above read the name as a question.

parody.text: Hengstenberg reads the cry of Revelation 13:4, “Who is like unto the beast?”, as “the derisive imitation of the name Michael”.

shield.text: In art his shield often bears the Latin “Quis ut Deus”, the name translated.

passages.title: One of the chief princes
passages.where: By the great river, the Hiddekel
passages.when: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia (Daniel 10:1)

key.text: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia.

around.text: Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words.
Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days.

says.text: A speaker sent to Daniel, who is not named, says that the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood him for twenty-one days, and that Michael, “one of the chief princes”, came to help him.
Daniel had been mourning “three full weeks” (10:2); the speaker says Daniel's words were heard “from the first day” (10:12). Three weeks are twenty-one days, the length of the withstanding.

passages.title: Michael your prince
passages.where: The same vision, as the speaker leaves

key.text: But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince.

around.text: Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.
Also I in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him.

says.text: The speaker will return to fight with the prince of Persia, and “the prince of Grecia shall come”. None holds with him in these things “but Michael your prince”.

passages.title: The great prince which standeth
passages.where: The close of Daniel's last vision
passages.when: Daniel 12, the last chapter of the vision

key.text: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.

around.text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

says.text: Michael is “the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”. At that time he “shall stand up”, there shall be a time of trouble such as never was, and Daniel's people shall be delivered, every one found written in the book.

passages.title: The Lord rebuke thee
passages.when: Looking back to the death of Moses (Deuteronomy 34)

key.text: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.

around.text: Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.
But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.

says.text: Michael is called “the archangel”. Contending with the devil, he disputed about the body of Moses, and did not bring a railing accusation, but said, “The Lord rebuke thee.”
Jude uses Michael's restraint as a contrast with men who “speak evil of dignities” (verse 8).

passages.title: War in heaven
passages.where: A vision of signs in heaven

key.text: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,
And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven.
And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.

around.text: And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.

says.text: There was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon fought and his angels, and prevailed not.
The dragon is named in the next verse: “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”. He was cast out into the earth, and his angels with him.

fromText.text: The name Michael is given to this being in five verses of the King James Bible: Daniel 10:13, 10:21 and 12:1, Jude 9 and Revelation 12:7.
Ten other verses use the same name for men: Numbers 13:13; 1 Chronicles 5:13, 5:14, 6:40, 7:3, 8:16, 12:20, 27:18; 2 Chronicles 21:2; Ezra 8:8.
The word “archangel” occurs twice in the King James Bible: once unnamed (1 Thessalonians 4:16) and once of Michael (Jude 9).
The titles the text gives him: “one of the chief princes”, “your prince”, “the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”, “the archangel”, and the leader of “his angels”.

notSaid.text: None of the five passages describes what Michael looks like.
“Chief princes” is plural and unnumbered. Scripture gives no list of angel ranks and no count of archangels.
The speaker who meets Daniel in chapter 10 is never named.
The prince of Persia and the prince of Grecia are not described beyond “withstood”, “fight” and “shall come”.

context.title: Daniel's last vision
context.lead: Daniel 10 to 12 is set by one river: the man clothed in linen is still there in 12:5–7. Michael is named twice in chapter 10 and once in 12:1.

claims.text: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, Daniel mourned three full weeks, eating no pleasant bread.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, by the great river Hiddekel, he saw “a certain man clothed in linen”; the men with him did not see the vision.
Keil identifies the Hiddekel as the Tigris.
Gabriel is named earlier in the book, in Daniel 8:16 and 9:21. He is not named in chapters 10 to 12.

verses.text: In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks.
And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel;
Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:

context.title: The prince of Persia and the prince of Grecia
context.lead: The text sets Michael beside two other “princes” that it does not describe.

claims.text: “The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days.”
“Now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.”
The speaker adds that in the first year of Darius the Mede he stood “to confirm and to strengthen him”.

verses.text: Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.

context.title: The archangel title
context.lead: “Archangel” is a New Testament word. It appears twice, and only once with a name.

claims.text: “The Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel.” This archangel is not named.
Thayer defines the Greek word as “chief of the angels … or one of the princes and leaders of the angels”, citing Daniel 10:13.

verses.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:

context.title: The captain of the LORD's host
context.lead: Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword near Jericho. The text does not name him.

claims.text: He says, “as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come”, and Joshua falls on his face and worships.
Identifying this captain with Michael is a view (see the questions).

verses.text: And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?
And the captain of the LORD’s host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

context.title: “The Lord rebuke thee” before Jude
context.lead: The words Michael speaks in Jude 9 are spoken by the LORD to Satan in Zechariah 3:2.

claims.text: “And the LORD said unto Satan, The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan.”
Calvin noted the same words in Zechariah when commenting on Jude 9.
Of Moses' burial the text says only that “he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab” and that “no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day”.

verses.text: And the LORD said unto Satan, The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.

echoes.text: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?
echoes.who: Moses and Israel, after the sea

echoes.text: For who in the heaven can be compared unto the LORD? who among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the LORD?
O LORD God of hosts, who is a strong LORD like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?
Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy.
And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast: and they worshipped the beast, saying, Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?

questions.q: Is Michael an angel, or Christ before his birth?
questions.text: The text calls him “one of the chief princes” (Daniel 10:13), “the archangel” (Jude 9), and the leader of “his angels” (Revelation 12:7). It does not say more about what he is.
questions.order: Holders are listed by the date they wrote.

views.view: He is Christ, the Word, before his birth

holders.quote: Michael may mean an angel; but I embrace the opinion of those who refer this to the person of Christ, because it suits the subject best to represent him as standing forward for the defense of his elect people.
holders.note: On Daniel 12:1. On 10:13 he leaves the question “in doubt for the present”.

holders.quote: According to one view, Michael is no other than Christ, or more correctly expressed, the Word, who in the beginning was with God … The following reasons decide in favour of the first view.

views.view: He is a created angel, one of the highest

holders.quote: This moderation, befitting only in a creature, certainly indicates a created angel.
holders.note: On Jude 9, as quoted (and answered) by Hengstenberg, 1851.

holders.quote: The first title points undoubtedly to an arrangement of orders and degrees among the angels, designating Michael as one of the most distinguished of the angel-princes.
This language suits an archangel rather than the Divine Son.
holders.note: On Jude 9. He adds that “the connection of M. with the Son of God in name and some functions is intimate”.

questions.q: Who is “the prince of the kingdom of Persia”?
questions.text: The text says only that he “withstood” the speaker for twenty-one days, and that the speaker will “fight” with him (Daniel 10:13, 20).
questions.order: Holders are listed by the date they wrote.

views.view: A human ruler: the king of Persia

holders.quote: The prince, says he, of the kingdom of the Persians, meaning Cambyses …

views.view: A spirit-being standing behind the kingdom

holders.quote: This spirit of the kingdom of Persia, whom, after the example of Jerome, almost all interpreters call the guardian angel of this kingdom, is as little the nature-power of this kingdom as Michael is the nature-power of Israel, but is a spirit-being.

questions.q: Where does Jude's dispute over the body of Moses come from?
questions.text: Deuteronomy says “he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab” and that no man knows his grave (34:6). It says nothing of Michael or the devil. Jude 9 does not name a source.
questions.order: Holders are listed by the date they wrote.

views.view: From a Jewish book, the Assumption of Moses

holders.quote: When Michael, the archangel, disputing with the devil, debated about the body of Moses. Here he confirms the assumption of Moses.

… in the work entitled The Ascension of Moses (a little treatise, of which the Apostle Jude makes mention in his Epistle), the archangel Michael, when disputing with the devil regarding the body of Moses …
Thus St. Jude 9 is derived from the latter.
holders.note: “The latter” is the lost ending of the book, the Assumption proper.

views.view: From an older tradition handed down among the Jews

holders.quote: Since the Jews at that time had many things from the traditions of the fathers, I see nothing unreasonable in saying that Jude referred to what had already been handed down for many ages.

questions.q: Is Michael the angel of the LORD, the captain of the LORD's host?
questions.text: Joshua 5:13–15 does not name the captain. Daniel 10 does not name the man clothed in linen.
questions.order: Holders are listed by the date they wrote.

views.view: Yes: Michael is the angel of the LORD and the captain of the host

holders.quote: In that passage of Jude, Michael speaks expressly as the “archangel,” as the captain of the Lord's hosts, as the angel of the Lord.

views.view: No: Michael is distinct from the angel of the LORD

holders.quote: The opinion … that the angel of the Lord who here appears to Daniel in divine majesty is identical with the angel-prince Michael, has no support in Scripture, and stands in contradiction to vers. 13 and 21.

questions.q: What does the question in his name point to?
questions.text: The name is a question: “Who is like God?” The same question is asked of God in Exodus 15:11, Psalm 89:6–8 and Micah 7:18, and turned toward the beast in Revelation 13:4.
questions.order: Holders are listed by the date they wrote.

views.view: Away from himself: no one is like God

holders.quote: the name denotes the infinite distance from God, “the humility of this distinguished angel, and his freedom from all self-elation”
holders.note: As reported by Hengstenberg, 1851, who rejects it.

views.view: To God's unmatched power at work through him

holders.quote: In the name: Who is like God, there must be supplied: Whose glory is represented in me.
The name … expresses, after the analogy of Ex. xv. 11, Ps. lxxxix. 7 f., the idea of God's unparalleled helping power.

tradition.title: 1 Enoch 20: seven holy angels
tradition.text: A Jewish book outside the Bible lists seven “holy angels who watch”, Michael among them. Charles counts chapters 12–36 among the book's oldest, pre-Maccabean, parts.
tradition.quote: Michael, one of the holy angels, to wit, he that is set over the best part of mankind [and] over chaos.

tradition.title: 1 Enoch 40: four presences
tradition.text: In the part Charles calls the Parables, Enoch sees four “presences” around the Lord of Spirits: Michael, Raphael, Gabriel and Phanuel.
tradition.quote: This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering.

tradition.title: The Assumption of Moses
tradition.text: A Jewish book whose ending is lost. Charles rebuilt that ending from quotations in Greek writers: Michael is sent to bury Moses, the devil opposes him, and Michael answers, “The Lord rebuke thee.”

tradition.title: Clement of Alexandria on Jude
tradition.text: The earliest Christian writer here to link Jude 9 with the Assumption of Moses.
tradition.quote: Here he confirms the assumption of Moses.

tradition.title: Origen, De Principiis
tradition.text: Origen names the book Jude used and reports another thing Michael says in it.
tradition.quote: the archangel Michael, when disputing with the devil regarding the body of Moses, says that the serpent, being inspired by the devil, was the cause of Adam and Eve's transgression.

tradition.title: The rabbis on the name
tradition.text: The Jewish Encyclopedia reports that the Talmudic teachers heard the name in Exodus 15:11, and that Simeon ben Lakish said the names of the angels came back with the Jews from Babylon.

tradition.title: Nine ranks of angels
tradition.text: The Celestial Hierarchy, written under the name of Dionysius, arranges nine kinds of heavenly beings in three orders. Archangels sit in the lowest order, between Principalities and Angels. Scripture gives no such list.
tradition.quote: the Word of God has assigned our Hierarchy to Angels, naming the distinguished Michael as Ruler of the Jewish people

tradition.title: Monte Gargano
tradition.text: The Catholic Encyclopedia reports an appearance of Michael at Monte Gargano in Italy, “as related in the Roman Breviary”, and a feast on 8 May.

tradition.title: Unnamed angels named Michael
tradition.text: “According to the Fathers”, Michael was also the cherub at the gate of paradise, the angel who stood against Balaam, and the angel who routed Sennacherib's army. Scripture names none of these angels.

tradition.title: Michaelmas, 29 September
tradition.text: The Gregorian Sacramentary keeps the dedication of a basilica of St Michael on 29 September. His feast on that day is Michaelmas: in England one of the quarter-days for settling rents and accounts.

tradition.title: Mont-Saint-Michel
tradition.text: Michael “is said to have appeared there, in 708, to St. Aubert, Bishop of Avranches”; the first church was dedicated on 16 October 710.

tradition.title: Where does he rank?
tradition.text: Opinions differ, the Catholic Encyclopedia says: Basil and other Greek Fathers place Michael over all the angels; Thomas Aquinas makes him prince of the lowest choir.

rev12.text: And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars:
And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.
And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.

And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.
And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne.
And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days.
And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,
And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven.
And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.

And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.
And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.

Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them. Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.

dan10.text: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks.
I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled.
And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel;
Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:

His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
And I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, so that they fled to hide themselves.
Therefore I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me: for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.
Yet heard I the voice of his words: and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I in a deep sleep on my face, and my face toward the ground.
And, behold, an hand touched me, which set me upon my knees and upon the palms of my hands.

And he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling.
Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words.
But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia.
Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days.
And when he had spoken such words unto me, I set my face toward the ground, and I became dumb.

And, behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.
For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither is there breath left in me.
Then there came again and touched me one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me,

And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me.
Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.
But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince.
Also I in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him.
